Article.ArticleTitle: Aerobic exercise and blood pressure: a meta-analysis of randomized trials.

Abstract.AbstractText: Elevated blood pressure is a leading modifiable risk factor for cardiovascular disease, and structured exercise programs are commonly recommended as a first-line intervention.
We pooled data from randomized controlled trials comparing supervised aerobic exercise against usual care, measuring change in systolic and diastolic blood pressure.

Aerobic exercise programs were associated with a mean reduction in systolic blood pressure of several millimeters of mercury, with more pronounced effects in participants who began with higher baseline readings.

Article.ArticleTitle: Sleep duration and metabolic markers: a systematic review.

Abstract.AbstractText: To systematically review studies relating habitual sleep duration to fasting glucose, insulin sensitivity, and lipid profiles in adults.

Short sleep duration, generally under six hours per night, was consistently associated with worse markers of glucose regulation across the reviewed studies, while long sleep duration showed more inconsistent associations.

Article.ArticleTitle: Recommended intervals for lipid screening in average-risk adults.

Abstract.AbstractText: This guideline addresses how frequently average-risk adults should undergo lipid panel screening.

For average-risk adults with a normal baseline lipid panel, rescreening at an interval of roughly every four to six years is reasonable, with shorter intervals for those with borderline results or new risk factors.

Article.ArticleTitle: Dietary fibre supplementation and LDL cholesterol: a randomized controlled trial.

Abstract.AbstractText: Soluble fibre has been proposed to lower LDL cholesterol by binding bile acids in the gut.
Participants with elevated LDL cholesterol were randomized to a daily soluble fibre supplement or a matching placebo for twelve weeks.
The fibre group showed a modest but statistically significant reduction in LDL cholesterol compared with placebo, with no significant change in HDL cholesterol.

Article.ArticleTitle: Exercise and heart rate variability: a narrative overview.

Abstract.AbstractText: This narrative review summarizes the physiological mechanisms by which regular aerobic exercise is thought to influence resting heart rate and heart rate variability.
Increased vagal tone following sustained training is a commonly cited mechanism, though the review notes substantial heterogeneity across the studies discussed and does not attempt a pooled estimate.

Article.ArticleTitle: Resting heart rate and long-term outcomes in a community cohort.

Abstract.AbstractText: A community-based cohort was followed over several years, with resting heart rate measured at baseline via standard clinic assessment.

Participants in the highest baseline resting heart rate group showed a higher observed rate of adverse cardiovascular events than those in the lowest group, an association that persisted after adjustment for common confounders.

Journal.Title: Synthetic Case Reports in Sleep Medicine

Article.ArticleTitle: Unusual presentation of sleep-related bruxism affecting daytime blood pressure readings: a case report.

Abstract.AbstractText: We describe a single patient presenting with elevated morning blood pressure readings that were ultimately attributed to severe, previously undiagnosed nocturnal bruxism disrupting sleep architecture.
Following treatment of the bruxism with a fitted oral appliance, the patient's morning blood pressure readings normalized over subsequent follow-up visits.

Article.ArticleTitle: Effect of a proprietary supplement on LDL cholesterol: a randomized controlled trial (retracted).

Abstract.AbstractText: A proprietary plant-sterol supplement was tested for its effect on LDL cholesterol in adults with moderately elevated baseline levels.
The supplement group showed a large reported reduction in LDL cholesterol relative to placebo over eight weeks of follow-up.
